reading:
This looks like a mid-sized neighbourhood supermarket with an Eastern European focus. It is larger than a corner shop but not a big chain store. A row of about five or six checkout counters with mint-green fronts runs down the left side. A long refrigerated wall case lines the right side, and the centre is filled with produce displays built from cardboard boxes on wooden pallets.

At the front, the produce includes a bin of yellow apples, melons, red apples in boxes printed "Watermelons", stacked green trays of clamshell tomatoes, cut watermelon halves and citrus. One dairy aisle has refrigerated shelves of tubs, probably sour cream, along with packs labelled "Tvorog" and wrapped cheese blocks. Across from it are boxed "Napoleonka" cakes and bags of Kirieshki croutons. Below those is a chest freezer of loose dumplings, with handwritten tags for "Chicken dumplings" and "Siberian dumplings" at $4.79. Another aisle pairs a cooler of sausages, salami and sliced cold cuts with shelves of small jars and tins, possibly fish or caviar, and red cans in a box at the end. One shelf run holds Kinder bars, Knoppers, Nestlé Crunch, Nutella, M&M's, Goralki wafers, gift tins, bottles that look like sparkling drinks, and a stand of lollipops and toys. I couldn't read the labels on the bottles or on the jars and tins.

Signs hang from the ceiling but are too small to read. The floor is pale tile, the ceiling has white panels with long strip lights, and the shelving is white.
